content.text: {"verdict":"major_issues","summary":"The siRNA, INTERFERin and cell-number scaling to 96-well is arithmetically consistent (about 27 nM siRNA, 73 µL final volume, 5,000 cells per well). The order of transfection, hypoxia start at 24 h, and lysis inside the workstation also follows the paper. The main problem is that the protein-normalisation step is probably not workable at this scale. Several smaller layout and handling problems could confound the siRNA comparison or the luciferase signal.","issues":[{"step":45,"severity":"major","issue":"Bradford normalisation is probably not feasible at this scale. By my estimate (not stated in the paper), 5,000 cells yield about 1–1.5 µg protein, so a 40 µL lysate is roughly 0.03 mg/mL. Only 5 µL of that goes into the assay, giving about 0.15 µg protein. This is below the lowest non-zero BSA standard (0.05 mg/mL, steps 50–51) and near or below the sensitivity of the Bradford dye method. The paper normalises luciferase to Bradford protein, so a noisy or undetectable protein readout would invalidate the normalisation.","suggestion":"Raise the protein signal. Options: seed more cells per well, lyse in 20 µL PLB (the Promega 96-well volume), use more lysate per Bradford well (for example 20 µL with proportionally adjusted dye), or extend the standard curve downward. Alternatively, use a more sensitive protein assay and state the deviation from the paper. Run a pilot check that sample absorbance falls inside the standard curve."},{"step":13,"severity":"minor","issue":"The layout puts all control siRNA in row A, an outer edge row of the plate, and the KDM2B siRNAs in rows B and C. Combined with 73 µL medium per well for 48 h (24 h of it in the dry workstation), evaporation and edge effects would be confounded with siRNA identity. Column 1 (U2OS) is also an edge column. The assumptions acknowledge that edge effects are not mitigated.","suggestion":"Move the experimental block to interior wells, or fill all unused surrounding wells with PBS or medium. Alternatively interleave the siRNA conditions across rows and seal the plates."},{"step":22,"severity":"minor","issue":"The three replicate wells per condition (adjacent columns) all come from one cell suspension and one transfection mix, so they are technical replicates. The paper reports n=3 biological replicates (Fig. 1B). The layout assumption calls them biological replicates.","suggestion":"Relabel the wells as technical replicates, and state that the experiment must be repeated independently three times, with separate cell preparations and transfections, to match n=3 biological replicates."},{"step":52,"severity":"minor","issue":"Luciferase Assay Reagent is added to all 54 wells in bulk and the plate is then read for several minutes (about 12 s per well). Signal decays after reagent addition, so reading order would bias the results. The note itself prefers injector or row-by-row dispensing, but the step as written does not do this.","suggestion":"Specify reagent addition by injector, or dispense and read one row or column at a time with a constant interval. Also randomise or interleave conditions across the read order. Consider adding PLB-only blank wells for luminescence background."},{"step":35,"severity":"minor","issue":"PBS_reservoir and PLB_1x_tube are used for both the bench (normoxia) plate and the hypoxia-workstation plate (steps 35, 37, 39, 41). One container cannot be in both places. Pre-equilibrated aliquots for the workstation are only mentioned in notes, not as explicit steps or containers.","suggestion":"Add separate containers for the workstation PBS and PLB. Add explicit steps to aliquot them into the workstation well ahead of lysis, and add a waste container inside the workstation."}]}
